newsitem.title: UK: INTERVIEW-BPB stg still biting Q1 profit.
newsitem.headline: INTERVIEW-BPB stg still biting Q1 profit.

text.p: BPB Plc, the UK building materials group, said on Thursday that sterling strength was continuing to squeeze profits into the current year, with the pound taking a five million stg bite out of profits for the first three months alone.

Jean-Pierre Cuny, chief executive, told Reuters in an interview "It's difficult to read ahead. But in the first three months the impact has been five million (stg)." Around 65 percent of the group's sales are sensitive to sterling levels, he said. Cuny added that BPB had hedging protection last year but was "still debating the future policy" on how to shield itself ahead.

He said the pound's surge since last summer had a commercial impact on its paperboard business, which is a major exporter and saw a 25 percent collapse in operating profits in the results published earlier.
Selling prices had been falling faster than input costs for recycled fibre as competition in Europe hotted-up due to the pound's value.
But the stg exposure was much more muted on the building materials side, which saw profits up 7.8 percent.

Asked how BPB planned to tackle the paperboard problem this year, with sterling's strength unabated, Cuny said: "It puts additional pressure on our restructuring. We have kept the division under review. We would like it not to worsen further."
The group was more upbeat about prospects for building materials and especially plasterboard, which saw its margins improve by one percent last year.
Cuny said he was hopeful of raising long term penetration in key plasterboard markets around the world.
Latest European plasterboard demand per capita figures showed particular scope for growth in the Spanish, Italian and Eastern European markets, said Cuny.

In Europe generally, long term annual demand growth of four to five percent looks set to hold, but product penetration still averages less than 50 percent of the estimated potential market in the UK, France and Germany, the annual statement said.
The group plans to maintain a robust programme of capital expenditure. Cuny said BPB had earmarked 450 million pounds to be spent over the coming three years.
